edk2-stable202208.byte_identical_replay_builds: permitted for recorded Radxa vendor releases when exact vendor artefacts, timestamps, and signing certificate inputs are supplied
edk2-stable202208.notes: This is the vendor baseline EDK2 release and remains the only supported exact-replay policy family.

post-edk2-stable202208.byte_identical_replay_builds: not valid after the EDK2 implementation is rebased
post-edk2-stable202208.notes: Post-202208 builds are deterministic source materialisations, but not byte-identical replays of the original vendor firmware.

latest.description: Build the latest maintained EDK2/Radxa source combination without opinionated firmware fixes unless they are explicitly enabled.

upstream.description: Rebuild and byte-compare the latest published Radxa firmware from its exact EDK2 202208 source and recorded replay inputs.

rules: config/refs-*.json records expected object IDs and tree IDs where those values are not derived
scripts compare immutable refs against manifests before use
unmanifested refs under immutable namespaces cause an abort outside integration workflows
if an immutable ref moved outside integrate-source-release, abort
if an immutable ref is checked out in a dirty worktree, abort
only integrate-source-release may create or advance immutable refs
integration updates the relevant manifest in the same operation
ordinary build targets never rewrite mutable source/unofficial/<line>/current refs or immutable Unofficial release checkpoints
source/cache/base/edk2/** refs are generated EDK2 component skeleton caches rather than irreducible source inputs
a pruned clone may omit source/cache/base/edk2/** branches when config/refs-edk2.json and the referenced component refs are present
generated skeleton tree IDs are derived from the referenced EDK2, edk2-platforms, and edk2-non-osi component refs
generated skeleton commits are validated by tree ID rather than object ID because commit metadata may differ after regeneration

requirements: source/cache/release/** refs are generated firmware artefacts, not irreducible source inputs.
A pruned clone may omit source/cache/release/** branches when all source/base, applicable source/vendor and/or source/port, and source/unofficial refs needed to regenerate them are present.
Generated release commits are validated by tree ID rather than object ID because commit metadata may differ after regeneration.
Rendered branches must adhere to conventional Git UX over exact retention of stale .gitmodules files.
Rendered branches must contain no gitlinks or active root .gitmodules files.
Submodule metadata is retained in manifests/reports, not as active submodule state.
Normal git log <path> and git blame <path> must work from any directory inside the repo.
Rendered branches are produced from render steps derived from available source refs and the selected source/cache/release branch name.
Versioned unofficial rendered source targets are aliases of the matching canonical /unofficial rendered source target for the same EDK2/CIX/Radxa tuple.
Nested .gitmodules files inside upstream source trees may remain as inert source files when no gitlink points at them.
If gitlinks remain after configured render steps, the renderer recursively materialises them using recorded .gitmodules URL mappings before validation.

committed_data: source refs and manifests needed to regenerate rendered buildable release branches
base component refs needed by supported releases
vendor component refs, vendor source refs, ported vendor source refs, and unofficial source branches
non-public or fragile vendor blobs, tools, and certificates
self_contained_source_policy.goal: The repository must contain everything required to build supported firmware even if external upstream remotes disappear.
remote_access: ordinary builds use local cache refs first when present, otherwise generate them from available source refs
external upstream/vendor repos are contacted only for integration or rendering when required objects are missing
if an external repo is unavailable, proceed when required refs and objects are already local
fail only when required data is unavailable locally and remotely

rules: unofficial release tags mark full unofficial source branches for each supported EDK2 release
each unofficial release tag must be reachable from its matching retained source/unofficial/edk2-stable* branch
tag names must not exactly duplicate branch names
base, CIX, and Radxa source versions are recorded as branches plus config refs metadata; duplicating them as tags is optional and not required by the build model
